title: Synthetic webshell written by the IIS worker into aspnet_client and then used

provenance.method: Fictional IIS and Sysmon rows written for this corpus; the file write is graded as the webshell-write tagger rule grades it.

seedEvents.description: IIS log on WEB-02: POST /ecp/DDI/DDIService.svc/SetObject from 198.51.100.23 returned 200
IIS log on WEB-02: POST /aspnet_client/system_web/error.aspx from 198.51.100.23 returned 200
Sysmon Process Create (EID 1) - ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\w3wp.exe - Image=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe - CommandLine=cmd.exe /c whoami @ WEB-02

findings.confidenceReason: The IIS worker wrote error.aspx, the same file was then POSTed to, and the worker spawned a shell one second later.
findings.title: Webshell error.aspx written by w3wp.exe and used on WEB-02
findings.description: w3wp.exe created C:\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\system_web\error.aspx; 198.51.100.23 then posted to it and w3wp.exe spawned cmd.exe /c whoami.

cannedOutput.attackerPath: 198.51.100.23 caused the IIS worker on WEB-02 to write the webshell error.aspx, then used it to run commands.
cannedOutput.summary: A webshell was written and used on WEB-02. The exact vulnerability that let the worker write it is inferred from one ECP request.

nextSteps.action: Acquire error.aspx from WEB-02 and record its hash and content
nextSteps.rationale: Confirms what the webshell does and gives a hash to hunt for.

uncertainties.basis: A POST to the ECP DDIService endpoint preceded the write by one minute.
uncertainties.gap: No request body or patch level for WEB-02 was collected.

forbiddenConclusions.claim: The attacker obtained domain administrator credentials or compromised the domain controller.
